ops.title: Swift BrokerSocketBridge treats EAGAIN as fatal — connected-socket handoff and notification consumer fail on errno 35
ops.description:
Found 2026-07-26 on the local machine immediately after the captain-hook helper first bootstrapped (fleet-stabilization pass, task fc39f885). With the helper running and stable, the client handshake improved from ECONNREFUSED to `bridge failed: disconnected` — and the cause is daemonkit's Swift half, not captain-hook:

```
01:52:52.654 [com.yasyf.daemonkit:BrokerSocketBridge] connected socket handoff failed: systemCall(operation: "read", errno: 35)
01:53:08.529 [com.yasyf.daemonkit:BrokerSocketBridge] connected socket handoff failed: systemCall(operation: "read", errno: 35)
01:53:21.918 [com.yasyf.daemonkit:BrokerSocketBridge] connected socket handoff failed: systemCall(operation: "read", errno: 35)
```

(os_log entries matching three client retries exactly.) errno 35 is EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK — a non-blocking read with no data ready, treated as fatal during the connected-socket handoff instead of waiting for readability. Sites: Sources/DaemonKit/BrokerHandoff.swift — logger category "BrokerSocketBridge" at :100, class BrokerSocketBridge at :295.

Second occurrence, same shape, different loop: the helper's notification consumer fails every ~11s with `notification consumer failed: systemCall(operation: "read", errno: 35)`, degrading to `deadlineExceeded` after display sleep. Two independent call sites → the EAGAIN handling is systemic in the Swift socket layer, not one bad read.

Diagnosability gap (own criterion): both host and helper plists point StandardOutPath/StandardErrorPath at capt-hookd.log, yet the entire failure is invisible there — the host file log shows zero lines in the failure window and zero lifetime hits for bridge/disconnect/codesign. Two diagnosis rounds read a healthy daemon from the file log while os_log held the answer.

Scope note: hook dispatch is unaffected (dispatches live throughout); the bridge failure gates the helper handshake ok=True and helper-fed features. Not fleet-convergence-blocking, but it is the last defect standing between the local machine and a fully green captain-hook.

ops.text: Non-blocking reads in the Swift socket bridge wait for readability on EAGAIN instead of failing the handoff
captain-hook helper handshake reaches ok=True on the local machine (was: bridge failed: disconnected)
Bridge/handoff failures are visible in the file log, not only os_log
